mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates fall.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong export-led growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which typically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or during periods of simultaneous productivity acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes, or during periods of falling inflation expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a broad-based deterioration in household demand, which reduces near-term earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -0.5% AND HOUST monthly change < -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered months, or during periods of strong foreign demand offsetting domestic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or during periods of extraordinary fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1% combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals an early-cycle supply expansion with tight labor markets, which boosts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or during periods of rising input costs eroding margins.
